blocks.text: Alternativa Distribution Unveils New Acquisitions, Including Cannes Prize-Winner “Elephants in the Fog” and Berlinale Opener “No Good Men”
The latest slate includes award-winning films from Cannes, Venice, Berlin and Busan, as well as titles connected to the 2027 Academy Awards.

Alternativa Distribution, a non-profit distribution label of the global film initiative Alternativa , supported by mobility platform inDrive , has announced its latest acquisitions ahead of MIPCOM 2026 . The new slate includes Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize winner and Nepal’s official submission for the 99th Academy Awards, “ Elephants in the Fog ” (2026), directed by Abinash Bikram Shah , Berlinale 2026 opening film “ No Good Men ” (2026), directed by Shahrbanoo Sadat , “Lost Land” (2025), directed by Akio Fujimoto , and the Academy Award-nominated documentary “ Four Daughters ” (2023), directed by Kaouther Ben Hania .

Launched in July 2026, Alternativa Distribution aims to create a fairer distribution model for filmmakers from the Global South while expanding the international reach of films with strong social and cultural themes. The latest acquisitions bring the distributor’s catalogue to 14 titles during its first year of operation.
The new slate brings together films that have received recognition at major international festivals and awards ceremonies.

“Elephants in the Fog”, directed by Abinash Bikram Shah, won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. It is also Nepal’s official submission in the Best International Feature Film category for the 99th Academy Awards. Alternativa Distribution will represent the film in multiple territories across Asia and Latin America.

“No Good Men”, directed by Shahrbanoo Sadat, was selected as the opening film of the 2026 Berlin International Film Festival. The film is also among the titles submitted to German Films for consideration in the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards. Alternativa Distribution will handle multiple territories across Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, and Sub-Saharan Africa.

“Lost Land”, directed by Akio Fujimoto, received the Orizzonti Special Jury Prize at the 2025 Venice Film Festival, the Golden Yusr Award for Best Feature Film at the Red Sea International Film Festival, and the Nativa Award at the 2026 Alternativa Film Festival. Alternativa Distribution will represent the film across Southeast Asia, excluding Malaysia, as well as the Nordic countries, Poland and Portugal.

“Four Daughters”, directed by Kaouther Ben Hania, won the L’Oeil d’or for Best Documentary at the Cannes Film Festival and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature. The distributor will represent the film in multiple territories across Latin America and Asia.
A Fairer Distribution Model for Filmmakers

Alternativa Distribution focuses on exclusive, first-window regional and international non-theatrical distribution rights for scripted, documentary and animated feature films with strong social and cultural themes. Its model is designed to help filmmakers reach broadcasters, streaming platforms and educational institutions beyond the traditional festival circuit.

Under its fair-terms approach, the distributor offers filmmakers an upfront minimum guarantee alongside a share of revenues once distribution deals are signed. It also provides localization support and seeks to make acclaimed international titles available to buyers at accessible licensing fees. Income is reinvested to expand the distributor’s reach and support filmmakers and regional film industries across the Global South.

One of the four newly announced titles was previously recognized at the Alternativa Film Festival, a travelling event and industry initiative dedicated to supporting impact-driven cinema. The festival’s most recent edition took place in Medellín, Colombia, in April 2026, with the next edition planned for Africa in 2027.
Supporting Stories from the Global South

Avital Lavi, Head of Alternativa Distribution, said the new slate would expand the distributor’s international reach and bring more acclaimed films to buyers and audiences who might otherwise have limited access to them: “With our second film slate, we are expanding our global reach to give buyers and audiences access to even more exceptional, high-impact storytelling,” Lavi said. “Our latest acquisitions have already proven themselves on the world stage, from a Cannes prize-winner to acclaimed titles featured at Venice and Berlinale. We’re incredibly proud to represent them and look forward to getting them in front of broadcasters and streaming platforms, and by extension audiences, that might not have had the chance to see them otherwise.”

Arsen Tomsky, CEO and Founder of inDrive, highlighted the challenges filmmakers from the Global South face in reaching international audiences: “Exceptional filmmaking can come from anywhere, but access to international audiences remains hindered by a deeply unequal system,” Tomsky said. “Alternativa Distribution was created to challenge that imbalance. This slate has been carefully curated and showcases the high quality and transformative power of filmmaking from the Global South, and the positive impact these films can have when they reach wider audiences.” Tomsky added that building a portfolio of 14 titles in the distributor’s first year represents an important milestone in its mission to connect these stories with audiences worldwide.
